items.q: Weiss ring with flashes and a few floaters but no pigment or breaks needs what?
o: Same day peripheral check then reassurance for uncomplicated PVD
items.exp: Complete detachment without tear threatens little once retina verified intact; tear symptoms education with fellow eye review completes care. Pigment or curtain changes urgency.
items.kp: Ring floater, clean retina: check then reassure.

items.q: Tobacco dust pigment (Shafer sign) over inferior vitreous after flashes indicates what?
o: Retinal tear needing urgent laser barricade
items.exp: Retinal pigment epithelium liberated through break sediments inferiorly; laser surrounds tear before subretinal fluid spreads into detachment. Delay detaches macula.
items.kp: Tobacco dust inside: laser the tear today.

items.q: Sudden bilateral vitreous haemorrhage after subarachnoid bleed is which syndrome?
o: Terson with subhyaloid blood needing neuro and retinal care
items.exp: Intracranial pressure surge ruptures peripapillary capillaries; coma management precedes vitrectomy for non clearing blood while sieves exclude aneurysm rebleed.
items.kp: Brain bleed plus eye blood: Terson.

items.q: Sea fan neovascularisation with vitreous bleed in sickle cell disease needs what caution?
o: Avoid acidosis and hypoxia sickling triggers; laser sea fans with exchange care
items.exp: Sickling precipitates with deoxygenation so anaesthesia and surgery need hydration, oxygenation and haematology input; scatter laser ablates ischaemic drive.
items.kp: Sickle sea fans: laser gently, never sicken.

items.q: Asteroid hyalosis is distinguished from synchysis scintillans by which behaviour?
o: Asteroid balls move with vitreous and stay suspended; synchysis gold crystals settle inferiorly and swirl on movement
items.exp: Calcium soaps lodge in gel pockets while cholesterol shards sediment in liquefied vitreous; both spare vision and observe while cataract surgery proceeds around them.
items.kp: Suspended diamonds versus settling gold snow.

items.q: Vitreous cells with subretinal infiltrates and CNS signs in elderly suggests masquerade of what?
o: Primary vitreoretinal lymphoma needing biopsy with IL-10 studies
items.exp: Large B cell lymphoma masquerades as chronic vitritis unresponsive to steroids; diagnostic vitrectomy with cytology and CNS imaging directs methotrexate based therapy.
items.kp: Steroid proof vitritis plus brain signs: biopsy for lymphoma.

items.q: Leukocoria with microphthalmos and elongated ciliary processes unilaterally in infant is what?
o: Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous differing by small eye without calcification
items.exp: Failed hyaloid regression leaves fibrovascular stalk dragging ciliary body; small globe without calcific mass separates from tumour while surgery risks bleeding. Bilateral PHPV is rare.
r: Incorrect. Tumour grows normal sized eye.
items.kp: Tiny eye, white pupil, no calcium: PHPV.

items.q: Patient with gas tamponade after vitrectomy must avoid what and posture how?
o: Flying and nitrous anaesthesia; face down for macular holes
items.exp: Gas expands with altitude and nitrous, spiking pressure and detaching repairs; positioning closes breaks against tamponade until chorioretinal adhesion forms. Bracelets warn anaesthetists.
items.kp: Gas bubble aboard: stay grounded, face down.

items.q: Proliferative vitreoretinopathy after detachment repair signifies what?
o: Membrane growth redetaching retina, grading prognosis and reoperation planning
items.exp: Retinal pigment cells proliferate on both retinal surfaces contracting into folds; extensive PVR needs membrane peeling with oil tamponade and guarded prognosis.

items.q: Dense diabetic vitreous haemorrhage obscuring fundus for weeks with B scan flat retina is managed how?
o: Watch for spontaneous clearing with laser once visible; vitrectomy for non clearing or detachment
items.exp: Blood often settles inferiorly over weeks permitting panretinal photocoagulation; early vitrectomy suits type 1 diabetics, bilateral cases, or ghost cell pressure. Ultrasound excludes traction.
r: Correct. Watch then laser; cut if stuck.
items.kp: Diabetic blood usually settles: laser when seen.
